_comment: Benchmark registry for the eval-platform skill. This is the only place
benchmark names appear in the skill's code, so adding one is a data edit.
instances: size of the scored split, used for cost estimation.
choices:   inference requests issued per instance, on either provider -- this
registry serves the platform path too, where they are olmo_core
forward passes and not vLLM prompts. MCQ log-likelihood scoring
sends one per answer choice; generative tasks send one per
instance, so choices is 1 for them.
A COUNT OF REQUESTS AND NOT OF THEIR LENGTH, WHICH MAKES IT A POOR
COST PROXY ACROSS PROMPT FORMATS. A ':mc' variant registers the same
choices as its base task and is correct to: the option count did not
change. But its prompt carries every labelled option and is repeated
once per option, where cloze carries one option per request, so it
forwards several times the tokens for an identical count. vLLM's
prefix caching hides that; the olmo_core provider has none. Do not
read equal counts as equal cost -- see BENCHMARKS.md, 'mc_format
costs more than its request count says'.
split:     which split the olmo-eval task scores. Documented here so the
estimate can be checked against the task definition.
metrics:   metric keys the task emits in metrics.json. Tasks with more than
one get qualified column names in accuracy_wide.csv.
kind:      mcq or generative. Affects how to read the score and how the
prompt count relates to the instance count.
groups:    named sets, selectable with --group. 'default' is what runs when
neither --group nor --benchmarks is given. A group is either a
plain list of benchmark names, or an object with:
benchmarks -- the list, or
like       -- inherit another group's list, so the two cannot
drift apart when one is edited
limit      -- instances per benchmark, applied unless --limit
is passed explicitly
description-- shown in the log when the group is selected
aliases:   common wrong names, mapped to the real olmo-eval task name. Used
only to produce a helpful error; they are never runnable.
unsupported: names people ask for that cannot produce a score today, with
the reason. These are refused even under --allow-any-task,
because that flag bypasses this registry -- it cannot conjure a
task olmo-eval does not define. Without this table the run would
fail only after the checkpoint was fetched, converted and booted,
taking every valid benchmark in the same request down with it.
See BENCHMARKS.md for where these numbers come from and why these splits.

smoke.description: plumbing check: the default set at 2 instances per benchmark, not a measurement

mc_format.description: multiple choice prompting: the same questions with the options labelled in the prompt and one letter token scored per option -- a cross-check on the default curve, not a substitute for it

unsupported.trex: no task file exists, and no canonical evaluation split has been chosen
unsupported.factscore: no task file exists; also needs an LLM judge and a retrieval corpus
unsupported.simpleqa: the bare task sets no metrics and would score nothing; use the 'simpleqa:judge' variant, which needs an OpenAI key and outbound network

limit_unsafe.hellaswag: loads validation AND train when limited, then samples from the union
limit_unsafe.socialiqa: loads validation AND train when limited, then samples from the union
limit_unsafe.socialiqa:mc: loads validation AND train when limited, then samples from the union -- the variant changes the prompt, not the loader
